result.topic_en: Euler discusses residues modulo a divisor, including negative and improper residues, and how residues behave under addition, subtraction, multiplication by an integer, and products of numbers.
result.transcription:
20 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
152. Hinc divisore $b$ existente $=2$, formula numerorum imparium $2m+1$ etiam ita $2m-1$
repraesentari potest; atque si divisor $b$ sit $=3$, classis numerorum, qui per 3 divisi relinquunt
binarium, etiam formula $3m-1$ continetur; sicque omnes numeros in una harum trium formularum
$3m$, $3m+1$ et $3m-1$ contineri necesse est.
153. Quare si residua negativa admittere velimus, omnes formulas $mb\pm r$ ita repraesentare
poterimus, ut residuum $r$ semissem divisoris $b$ non superet. Si enim esset $r>\frac{1}{2}b$, pro $r$ sumamus
$-(b-r)$ eritque $b-r<\frac{1}{2}b$.
154. Simili modo cum sit $mb+r=(m-1)b+b+r$, residuo $r$ etiam aequivalet residuum
$b+r$, vocabulo in latiori sensu accepto. Generatim ergo residua minus proprie ita dicta $b+r$,
$2b+r$, $3b+r$, etc. aequivalent residuo $r$ proprie sic dicto.
155. Scilicet divisore existente $b$, omnis numerus, etiamsi sit major quam $b$, tanquam residuum
spectari potest, qui ad residuum proprie ita dictum reducetur, divisorem $b$ inde toties auferendo,
quoties fieri licet, quod adeo negativa admittendo infra semissem ipsius $b$ deprimi poterit.
156. Ita si divisor sit 6 et residuum 16, hoc residuum improprium reducetur ad proprium
4, atque adeo ad negativum $-2$, sive istae formulae $6m+16$, $6m+4$, $6m-2$ pro aequivalentibus sunt habendae, quia omnes numeri in una contenti simul in reliquis continentur.
157. Circa residua plures insignes proprietates perpendi oportet. Si numerus $A$ per divisorem
$d$ divisus, praebeat residuum $\alpha$, numeri quoque $A+d$, $A+2d$, $A+3d$, etc. idem relinquent
residuum $\alpha$, at numerus $A+1$ per eundem divisus dabit residuum $\alpha+1$, et generaliter numerus
$A+n$ residuum dabit $\alpha+n$, quod si excedat divisorem $d$, eo subtrahendo quoties fieri potest,
ad minimam formam reducetur.
158. Simili modo, si sumto divisore $d$, numero $A$ residuum conveniat $\alpha$, numeri quoque
$A-d$, $A-2d$, $A-3d$, etc. idem relinquent residuum, at numero $A-1$ residuum conveniet
$\alpha-1$, et numero $A-n$ residuum $\alpha-n$, quod si forte sit negativum, additione divisoris $d$ ad
positivum reducetur.
159. Sumto divisore $d$, si numero $A$ conveniat residuum $\alpha$, numero vero $B$ residuum $\beta$,
aggregato horum numerorum $A+B$ conveniet residuum $\alpha+\beta$, quod congruit cum $\alpha+\beta-d$,
si forte sit $\alpha+\beta>d$. Hinc patet si sit $\alpha+\beta=d$, fore $A+B$ multiplum ipsius $d$.
160. Iisdem positis, differentiae numerorum $A-B$ conveniet residuum $\alpha-\beta$, vel etiam
$\alpha-\beta+d$, si forte sit $\beta>\alpha$. Unde si sit $\alpha=\beta$, seu si numeri $A$ et $B$ paria relinquant residua,
eorum differentia erit per divisorem $d$ divisibilis.
161. Sumto divisore $d$, si numerus $A$ praebeat residuum $\alpha$, ejus duplum $2A$ dabit residuum
$2\alpha$, vel etiam $2\alpha-d$, triplum vero $3A$ dabit residuum $3\alpha$, cujus, si sit majus quam $d$, minima
forma erit vel $3\alpha-d$, vel $3\alpha-2d$. Atque in genere multipli cujusvis $nA$ residuum erit $n\alpha$,
sive $n\alpha-md$.
162. Si divisore posito $=d$, numero $A$ respondeat residuum $\alpha$, numero vero $B$ residuum $\beta$,
producto $AB$ residuum conveniet $\alpha\beta$, quod si forte majus fuerit quam divisor $d$, reducitur ad
$\alpha\beta-d$, vel $\alpha\beta-md$.

methods.what: Every integer lies in one of the classes 3m, 3m+1, 3m-1 (residues mod 3 with negative residue allowed)
methods.quote:
omnes numeros in una harum trium formularum
$3m$, $3m+1$ et $3m-1$ contineri necesse est

methods.what: Least absolute residue: with negative residues allowed, the residue can be taken at most half the divisor
methods.quote:
Si enim esset $r>\frac{1}{2}b$, pro $r$ sumamus
$-(b-r)$ eritque $b-r<\frac{1}{2}b$

methods.what: Residues r, b+r, 2b+r, ... are equivalent (congruence classes)
methods.quote:
residua minus proprie ita dicta $b+r$,
$2b+r$, $3b+r$, etc. aequivalent residuo $r$ proprie sic dicto

methods.what: Reduction of an improper residue by subtracting the divisor; example 16 mod 6 ≡ 4 ≡ -2
Residue of A+n is α+n; adding multiples of d leaves residue unchanged
Residue of A−n is α−n, made positive by adding d
methods.quote:
numero $A-n$ residuum $\alpha-n$, quod si forte sit negativum, additione divisoris $d$ ad
positivum reducetur

methods.what: Residue of a sum is the sum of residues; if α+β=d then d divides A+B
methods.quote: Hinc patet si sit $\alpha+\beta=d$, fore $A+B$ multiplum ipsius $d$

methods.what: Residue of a difference is the difference of residues; equal residues imply d divides A−B
methods.quote:
si numeri $A$ et $B$ paria relinquant residua,
eorum differentia erit per divisorem $d$ divisibilis

methods.what: Residue of nA is nα reduced by multiples of d
methods.quote:
in genere multipli cujusvis $nA$ residuum erit $n\alpha$,
sive $n\alpha-md$

methods.what: Residue of a product is the product of residues reduced mod d
methods.quote:
producto $AB$ residuum conveniet $\alpha\beta$, quod si forte majus fuerit quam divisor $d$, reducitur ad
$\alpha\beta-d$, vel $\alpha\beta-md$
